conventions.convention: The finite system has d ≥ 1; the Hermitian coupling family may be empty. H and H_LS have units joules, ℏ has units joule-seconds, β is any real inverse-energy parameter, and Γ has units inverse seconds.
S_a(ω) sums P_E S_a P_E′ over E′ − E = ℏω, so positive ω lowers energy. The generator places S_b(ω) on the left and S_a(ω)* on the right, with thermal balance γ_ab(−ω) = exp(−βℏω)γ_ba(ω).

Relative entropy uses natural logarithms and support-restricted spectral logarithms, with 0 log 0 = 0. The stationary reference σ is positive definite, so relative entropy is finite for every density matrix.

The logarithmic derivative formula is asserted only where ρ_t is positive definite, using a right derivative at t = 0. At singular states only the extended-real upper right Dini derivative is asserted to be nonpositive.
Stationarity and nonincrease of relative entropy imply neither uniqueness nor convergence. The counterexample uses H = 0, γ > 0, Z = diag(1,−1), and generator L(X) = γ(ZXZ − X), with time in seconds.

load_bearing.statement: For a finite exponential CPTP semigroup T_t with a faithful stationary density σ, t ↦ D(T_tρ‖σ) is nonincreasing for every density ρ. Where ρ_t is positive definite, its derivative is Tr(L(ρ_t)(log ρ_t − log σ)) ≤ 0, with a right derivative at zero; at singular states the upper right Dini derivative is at most zero.

Defines the finite energy-resolved generator from Hermitian H and S_a, positive semidefinite rate matrices satisfying γ_ab(−ω) = exp(−βℏω)γ_ba(ω), and Hermitian H_LS commuting with H, with the specified frequency sign, matrix ordering and SI units.

Under the stated finite thermal-generator hypotheses, σ_β = exp(−βH)/Tr(exp(−βH)) is faithful, T_t = exp(tL) is completely positive and trace-preserving for t ≥ 0, and T_t(σ_β) = σ_β. Neither uniqueness nor convergence is asserted.

seams_checked.note: Checked supplier statement and proof against the consuming theorem's A1 and step 1.1. The supplier establishes DPI for every finite CPTP map and positive semidefinite pair, including support-failure cases. The consumer applies precisely that direction to a finite channel and a faithful stationary reference. Natural-logarithm and support conventions agree. The supplier makes no converse, strict-decay, equality, recovery or convergence assertion, and the consumer imports none.
